text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate (us-west-2). Alerting: 502/504 spikes, p90 latency up. Pager: sam (oncall)

sam (oncall): seeing it. Routing errors and a handful of segfault traces in model-runner. Investigating.

maya: replicated a repro on a dedicated worker: model-runner process segfaults under heavy long-context requests (~32k tokens). Stack shows malloc/free noise.

jordan: throwing this here — customer A is reporting timeouts and failed requests in the last 10m. Can we triage customer impact?

ops-eng: customer impact: approx 2.8% of API calls failing (502/504) across the batch. Error spike started 14:12 PDT. Most failures map to inference nodes in us-west-2a.

sam (oncall): quick mitigations: 1) scale down long-context worker pool to 0 for now 2) route new requests to fallback model-variant small-latency (rw-small) 3) enable busy-loop watchdog to restart crashing runner. I'll roll these in that order.

beth: +1 on routing to fallback. Adding a temporary request-size throttle at the gateway for >16k token prompts. Patch queued.

maya: logs from a crashed runner (trimmed):
```
#0  0x7f8a1c2d in __libc_malloc
#1  0x55b2f1a3 in qkv_cache_alloc
#2  0x55b2d9b1 in attention_forward
#3  0x55b2c7e4 in model_step
#4  0x55b2b5f0 in runner_process_request
```
looks like a heap corruption path in quant attention kernel.

lee-sre: noted. This smells like a regression in the recent quantized-attn change (release 2026-03-05). Who can hotpatch the kernel?

jordan: I can prepare a rollback/hotpatch build. Propose: revert the specific commit (git sha: a1b2c3d4) that landed the new allocator heuristics and push a canary to 2 instances.

sam (oncall): doing actions now: 1) apply gateway throttle (deployed) 2) reroute traffic away from us-west-2a -> reducing load on bad AZ 3) starting canary with rollback build to 2 runners. ETA 3 minutes.

ops-eng: routing changes applied. Error rate dipped ~60% in first minute. Gateway throttle is blocking ~0.6% of requests (large prompts).

maya: canary logs show no segfaults on the reverted runner after 2m under similar load. Good sign.

beth: customer A contact: "errors still intermittent" but severity reduced. They asked for ETA.

sam (oncall): communicating: mitigation in progress, full rollback to roll-forward patch if canary holds. ETA 15-30m for full rollout.

jordan: initiating full flip once 15m of stable telemetry. Preparing automated rollout with 5% -> 25% -> 100% policy and automatic rollback on error spike.

ops-eng: telemetry: error rate now at baseline +0.4% (noise), p90 latency back to normal.

incidents-bot: Incident status: Mitigated (partial) — traffic reroute + canary rollback applied. Pager remains open for monitoring and postmortem.

sam (oncall): next steps: 1) finish rollout if stable 2) collect core dumps and heap-use-after-free traces from affected nodes 3) open incident PM with owner (maya) and timeline.

maya: will capture cores and run ASAN-style repro on isolated hardware. Suspect heap corruption introduced by quant allocator heuristics interacting with large KV-cache sizes.

beth: I'll follow up on customer comms and patch support ticket.

lee-sre: once cores available I'll run crash symbology and check for double-free paths; also recommend adding a short-term probe that rejects >24k token requests at the gateway for 48h.

sam (oncall): closing loop: full rollout started at 15:12 PDT, no regression for 20m; rolling to 100% now. Leaving incident as "monitoring".

incidents-bot: timestamped note: 8201234567 - Pager triggered; mitigations applied; rollback canary validated; full rollout initiated; postmortem pending.

jordan: filing postmortem with labels: inference, segfault, quant-kernel, hotpatch. Assign maya as lead.

beth: thanks all — will update customer A and mark support ticket as mitigated. :white_check_mark:
